clean.confirmRecycle: {0} files from {1} targets will be moved to the Trash. You can restore them later.
settings.language.desc: Interface language. Auto follows your macOS language.
settings.theme.desc: Pick a theme or follow macOS.
settings.backdrop.desc: Lets the desktop softly show through the window.
settings.deleteMode.recycle.desc: Safer. Files can be restored, but space is freed only after the Trash is emptied.
about.description: A fast, beautiful cache and junk cleaner for macOS. It scans well-known cache, log and leftover locations across the system, browsers, developer tools, apps and games, then lets you decide what goes.
about.safety.desc: Only files underneath scanned locations are ever touched. The system, your home folder, Documents, Desktop, Downloads, iCloud Drive and app containers are hard-blocked. Caches are deleted for good; what you remove by hand goes to the Trash.
insight.snapshots.title: Local Time Machine snapshots
insight.snapshots.detail: {0} is purgeable, mostly held by {1} local snapshots. macOS frees it by itself when space runs low; “tmutil thinlocalsnapshots” frees it now.
insight.purgeable.title: Purgeable space
insight.purgeable.detail: {0} is purgeable: iCloud copies and caches macOS can evict. It is freed automatically when space runs low.
insight.sleepimage.title: Sleep image
insight.sleepimage.detail: {0} reserved by the sleep image. On a desktop Mac, “sudo pmset -a hibernatemode 0” stops writing it.
insight.swap.title: Swap files
insight.swap.detail: {0} used by virtual memory. Managed by macOS; it shrinks after a restart or when memory frees up.
insight.simulators.title: Simulator devices
insight.simulators.detail: {0} in Xcode simulator devices. “xcrun simctl delete unavailable” removes the ones whose runtimes are gone.
insight.appleintelligence.title: Apple Intelligence models
insight.appleintelligence.detail: About {0} of on-device models. Turn Apple Intelligence off in Settings and macOS removes them.
insight.trash.title: Trash
insight.trash.detail: {0} is waiting in the Trash. Enable the Trash target to empty it.
target.mac.caches.name: App caches
target.mac.caches.desc: Caches apps keep in ~/Library/Caches. Rebuilt as you use them; Apple’s own are left alone.
target.mac.temp.name: Temporary files
target.mac.logs.name: Logs
target.mac.crashreports.name: Crash reports
target.mac.crashreports.desc: Diagnostic and crash reports written when apps fail.
target.mac.thumbnails.name: Quick Look thumbnails
target.mac.thumbnails.desc: Finder and Quick Look preview cache. Rebuilt on demand.
target.mac.savedstate.name: Saved app state
target.mac.savedstate.desc: Window positions apps restore at launch.
target.mac.iosbackups.name: iPhone & iPad backups
target.mac.iosbackups.desc: Local device backups made by Finder. Deleting them is permanent for those backups.
target.mac.trash.name: Trash
target.mac.trash.desc: Files waiting in the Trash. Emptying is permanent.
target.browser.safari.name: Safari
target.browser.arc.name: Arc
target.browser.arc.desc: HTTP, code, GPU and service-worker caches for all profiles.
target.app.teams.desc: Cache, code cache, GPU cache and logs.
target.dev.xcode.deriveddata.name: Xcode DerivedData
target.dev.xcode.deriveddata.desc: Build products and indexes. Xcode rebuilds them.
target.dev.xcode.devicesupport.name: Xcode device support
target.dev.xcode.devicesupport.desc: Debug symbols copied from every device and OS version you ever connected.
target.dev.xcode.archives.name: Xcode archives
target.dev.xcode.archives.desc: Archived app builds, including the dSYMs needed to read old crash logs.
target.dev.simulator.name: Simulator caches
target.dev.simulator.desc: Dyld and runtime caches of the iOS Simulator.
target.dev.homebrew.name: Homebrew downloads
target.dev.homebrew.desc: Bottles and source archives already installed.
target.dev.cocoapods.name: CocoaPods cache
target.dev.swiftpm.name: Swift Package Manager
target.dev.bun.name: Bun cache
target.game.metal.name: Metal shader cache
target.game.metal.desc: Compiled shaders. Games may stutter briefly while rebuilding.
space.mac.claudetmp.name: Claude Code scratch files
space.mac.claudetmp.desc: Output Claude Code saves while it works, one folder per project. Quit Claude Code before removing it.
space.kind.session.name: Project scratch files
space.kind.session.desc: What Claude Code saved while working on one project. Quit Claude Code before removing it.
space.mac.lima.name: Lima virtual machines
space.mac.lima.desc: Linux virtual machines run by Lima (and Colima). Delete the ones you no longer use with “limactl delete”.
space.mac.simulators.name: Simulator devices
space.mac.simulators.desc: Xcode simulator devices with their installed apps. The command removes the ones whose runtime is gone.
space.mac.vms.name: Virtual machines
space.mac.vms.desc: Parallels, VMware Fusion and VirtualBox virtual machines, one row per machine.
space.mac.uv.name: Pythons and tools installed by uv
space.mac.uv.desc: Python versions and command-line tools installed with uv. Remove the ones you don't use with “uv python uninstall” and “uv tool uninstall”.
space.mac.applications.name: Applications
space.mac.applications.desc: Apps in the Applications folder, one row per app. The trash icon uninstalls an app with its caches and data.
space.mac.aerial.name: Aerial wallpapers and screen savers
space.mac.aerial.desc: Downloaded Aerial videos for the wallpaper and the screen saver. Pick another wallpaper and screen saver first, then run the command in Terminal; macOS downloads them again if you choose Aerial later.
space.mac.installdata.name: Leftover macOS update
space.mac.installdata.desc: A macOS installer staged by Software Update. If no update is waiting, the command removes it; macOS downloads it again when needed.
space.mac.iosbackups.name: iPhone and iPad backups
space.mac.iosbackups.desc: Local device backups made by Finder, one row per device. Deleting one is permanent for that backup.
space.kind.device.name: Device backup
space.kind.device.desc: A backup of one iPhone or iPad. Make sure you have a newer one before removing it.
space.mac.trash.name: Trash
space.mac.trash.desc: Files waiting in the Trash. They take space until you empty it in Finder.
disk.mac.needsAccess: Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Music, Movies, iCloud Drive, Mail and the Trash are measured only with Full Disk Access; until then their space counts as System and other.
dash.binLine: Trash: {0} — turn on its target to empty it with the rest
clean.binBody: {0} items in the Trash will be deleted permanently. This cannot be undone.
settings.deleteMode.recycle.descWin: For what you remove by hand (the Disk page, the contents of a target): it can be restored, and frees space once the Trash is emptied. Caches are always deleted for good.
disk.filter.empty: No folder accounts for this space: macOS reports it in use by the system, the file system itself and places an ordinary app cannot read.
space.mac.sysvolumes.name: macOS and its volumes
space.mac.sysvolumes.desc: The system itself, its startup files, updates and virtual memory, each on a volume of its own. macOS manages them; open a row to see each one.
space.mac.sysfolders.name: System folders
space.mac.sysfolders.desc: Shared libraries, drivers, logs and temporary files of the system and of apps, outside your home folder. Kept by macOS and installed software.
space.mac.appcontainers.name: Other apps' containers
space.mac.appcontainers.desc: Data of sandboxed apps, in ~/Library/Containers and Group Containers. Remove it by uninstalling or cleaning inside the app.
space.mac.noaccess.name: Closed without Full Disk Access
space.mac.noaccess.desc: Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Music, Movies, iCloud Drive, the Trash, Mail and other apps' containers. macOS does not let the app read them, so they are counted together here. Grant access to see them folder by folder.
space.unknown.name: Not identified
space.unknown.desc: macOS reports this space in use, but no folder the app can read accounts for it: local snapshots, the file system's own records and places closed to every app.
access.ask.title: Give JunkCleanup Full Disk Access
access.ask.body: Instead of macOS asking about Photos, Music, Documents and each other folder one by one, one switch covers them all and shows the whole disk. Nothing protected is opened until then. Turn on JunkCleanup on the page that opens.
disk.uninstall.tip: Uninstall with its caches and data
disk.uninstall.title: Uninstall {0}? {1}
disk.uninstall.partly: {0} is in the Trash; {1} of its files stayed in place.
disk.uninstall.done: {0} and its data are in the Trash · {1}
disk.uninstall.row: The app itself. The trash icon removes it with its caches, settings and data.
